groups.reason: Duden independently identifies German Mut as courage/readiness and traces it through Middle and Old High German muot, denoting temperament, passion and resolve. This lexical noun is independent of the Latin mutare mutation family. Ten finite transparent noun compounds retain this complete terminal courage/temperament component and are excluded from family mut. Bare homographic names (Helmut, Hartmut, Almut), mammoth fragments, permutations, malformed spellings and different full lexical heads such as Anmut/Unmut/Gleichmut remain separate. No blanket rule for words ending in mut, no general national realization or additional family.
